source.reconstruction_note: The original generated case file was absent from the report archive. These ten approved case titles, prompts, and iteration-one corrections were reconstructed from the human-readable report.

cases.source_case: Positive 1 - Run the full pipeline with a local USD and download output
cases.prompt: Use the already running Physics Agent REST service to upload the public lightbulb USD, run the full pipeline, monitor it, and download predictions and the simulation-ready output USD.

expected.description: Checks GET /health, uses one input source, submits POST /pipeline, monitors the matching status route with a timeout, and names the prediction and output-USD downloads without starting containers.
Counts sessions from GET /sessions before and after, verifies exactly one new case-owned pipeline session completed, and confirms downloaded artifacts exist.

prerequisites: A Physics Agent service is already running and GET /health succeeds.
Any bearer token is available through PHYSICS_AGENT_TOKEN without exposing it.
The service VLM, rendering, optimizer, storage, and physics-authoring dependencies are healthy.
side_effects: Creates one service pipeline session and server-side artifacts.
Downloads predictions and an output USD into a case-specific temporary directory.
cleanup: Delete the case-owned service session with DELETE /sessions/{id}.
Remove case-specific downloads and leave the pre-existing service running.

cases.source_case: Positive 2 - Write a curl upload, watch, and download workflow
cases.prompt: Give me a robust curl and jq workflow to upload a USD to Physics Agent, watch events or poll status, handle terminal failures, and download the predictions, report, and output USD.

expected.description: Uses fail-fast curl flags, safely extracts the session ID with jq, monitors a documented route with a timeout, handles failed and cancelled states, and downloads only after completed.

cases.source_case: Positive 3 - Use the bundled Python client with an S3 URI
cases.prompt: Write a Python example using the bundled Physics Agent client to submit a user-provided S3 URI, monitor the pipeline, and download results without embedding cloud credentials.

expected.description: Uses s3_uri as the only source, leaves cloud credentials server-side, applies bounded monitoring and terminal-state handling, and does not invent or expose a real bucket URI.

cases.source_case: Positive 4 - Troubleshoot an instance-proxy authoring failure
cases.prompt: A Physics Agent service pipeline failed in apply_physics on an instance proxy. Explain how to distinguish a schema-authoring failure from an optimizer failure and construct the corrected request.

expected.description: Inspects the failed step and error, explains that deinstance addresses non-writable instance proxies, uses optimize_usd with enable_deinstance, and does not claim every apply_physics schema error is fixed by preprocessing.

cases.prompt: Use the Physics Agent service prediction-only API on a prepared case-owned pipeline session. Submit the correct fields, wait for completion, and return predictions without running apply_physics again.

expected.description: Uses the documented POST /predict request fields and matching predict status and results routes, and clearly distinguishes prediction-only work from POST /pipeline.

Uses GET /sessions to verify prediction reuses the existing session ID without creating another session, waits for it to complete, and retrieves non-empty predictions without asserting an authored output USD.

prerequisites: A healthy Physics Agent service and a completed case-owned pipeline session with prepared data are available.
The service VLM provider is configured for prediction.
The evaluator can query GET /sessions and the predict result routes.
side_effects: Mutates the case-owned pipeline session in place with prediction-only status and artifacts.
Downloads predict results into a case-specific temporary directory.
cleanup: Delete the case-owned pipeline session after the prediction-only run.
Remove downloaded results and leave the service running.

cases.prompt: Use the Physics Agent service tuning API on a physics-authored public tire USD, submit the drop-settle scenario with bounded trials, and return the best parameters and tuned USD.

expected.description: Requires a physics-authored source, uses POST /tune with the documented scenario and optimizer fields, bounds trials, follows tune status and result routes, and rejects a fake engine as production evidence.
Counts exactly one new tune session from GET /sessions, waits for terminal completion, and verifies best-parameter metadata and a downloadable tuned USD.

prerequisites: A healthy Physics Agent service has production tuning dependencies configured.
A case-owned physics-authored tire USD or completed pipeline session is available.
The evaluator has sufficient GPU and runtime capacity for bounded tuning.
side_effects: Creates one tune session and multiple bounded simulation trial artifacts.
Downloads best parameters, score evidence, and a tuned physics USD.
cleanup: Cancel the case-owned tune session on timeout and delete it after evidence collection.
Delete the case-owned source session and remove downloaded trial artifacts.

cases.source_case: Negative 1 - Run the local Physics Agent CLI
cases.prompt: There is no REST service. Run Physics Agent directly from the local command line on my USD.

expected.description: Routes to physics-agent-cli and does not invent a service endpoint or start containers.

cases.source_case: Negative 2 - Deploy the Physics Agent service with Docker
cases.prompt: The service is unreachable. Build and start the Physics Agent Docker Compose stack, then retry the API request.

expected.description: Reports the failed health preflight, makes zero service submissions and zero Docker mutations, and routes deployment to deploy-physics-agent-docker.

cases.source_case: Negative 3 - Make a Material Agent service request
cases.prompt: Upload this USD to a service that assigns realistic visual materials and download the materialized result.

expected.description: Routes to material-agent-client and does not present Physics Agent's output USD as visual material assignment.

cases.prompt: What do UsdPhysicsRigidBodyAPI and UsdPhysicsCollisionAPI represent?

expected.description: Answers the conceptual question directly without contacting a service or fabricating a session.
